newsitem.title: UK: UK's Ofgas opens inquiry into Goldfish credit card.
newsitem.headline: UK's Ofgas opens inquiry into Goldfish credit card.

text.p: Gas industry watchdog Ofgas said on Friday it had launched an anti-competitiveness investigation into the Goldfish credit card, launched last year by HFC Bank and gas supplier Centrica.
Ofgas is asking for comments to decide whether the credit card unfairly ties its holders to Centrica, which was spun off from British Gas through a demerger in February.
The Goldfish card, which was launched in September, gives holders the opportunity of a discount of up to 75 pounds on their gas bills.
Ofgas said an unnamed rival gas supplier recently complained after it met with a "prelimary negative response" when it wanted to join the Goldfish scheme.
The Goldfish credit card has attracted over 350,000 holders since its launch. Holders can also save points to get vouchers for purchases at ASDA Group Plc supermarkets or Boots Co Plc stores.
But Goldbrand, the company which markets the card, denied that it was anti-competitive.
"I cannot actually see how the Goldfish card is anti-competitive," a spokesman for Goldbrand said.
Goldfish card holders do not necessarily have to redeem their points with Centrica, while the company's rivals are free to set up their own schemes, he added.
But he confirmed that one competitor was denied to join the Goldfish scheme for the moment, because it would be uneconomical given the company's small customer base.
Access to the scheme for this firm would therefore result in disproportionally high administrative costs for Goldbrand, he said.
Centrica lost its monopoly in the British domestic gas market last year when competition was introduced in part of England. The market is expected to be fully opened around next year.
Rival gas suppliers and other interested parties can send responses to Ofgas by June 27, after which the regulator will decide whether to take further action.
